notes: The source is a Department of Revenue Administration press release. The Interest and Dividends Tax was New Hampshire's only tax on income (on interest and dividends); the release says taxpayers are no longer required to pay it for tax periods beginning on or after January 1, 2025. The brackets, surtaxes, deductions and reliefs are therefore empty.

Prior law (note only, not applicable to 2025): the release says the tax was 3% for periods ending on or after December 31, 2024, and applied only to periods through 2024; periods on or before December 31, 2024 remain subject to audit and collection.
The source prints no standard deduction, personal or dependent exemption, or other income-tax deduction (it describes no income tax in force for 2025).
Social Security treatment: not stated in the source; not found in the source.
The release does not mention pensions or retirement income; not found in the source.
Municipal bond interest treatment: not stated in the source; not found in the source.
Capital gains: the source prints no rate or treatment for gains; not found in the source.
The release is dated January 23, 2025 and is recorded as tax year 2025 as dispatched.
